newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open down before Greenspan testimony.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open down before Greenspan testimony.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened moderately lower before Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's much anticipated Congressional testimony.

Nervousness ahead of Greenspan's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony combined with the Treasury's auction of $12.5 billion in five-year notes this afternoon combined to keep prices under pressure, analysts said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was down 3/32 to 99-16/32, yielding 6.66 percent, in early dealings.
"We have seen a little bit of downward pressure this morning," said Kim Rupert, senior economist at MMS International.
Rupert attributed the pressure to anxiety before the Greenspan speech, supply considerations, and a weaker dollar versus the yen.
"The dollar has dropped a little on fears of Japanese repatriation at fiscal yearend," she noted.
Rupert said the market is divided on what the tone will be of Fed Chairman Greenspan's testimony.

"Our take on it is that Greenspan really can't say anything too friendly," said Rupert. "The economic data are on the strong side, with the exception of some very tame inflation numbers. That means his remarks should leave him slightly on the hawkish side."

But Rupert noted that some other people think that Greenspan will not say anything "too damaging" and that his remarks will be relatively friendly. Rupert said the market has more completely priced in the idea that Greenspan's testimony will be hawkish and that if that scenario does not materialize, the market could trade higher on relief.
How Greenspan goes, so goes the Treasury's five-year note auction, some analysts said.
Greenspan is scheduled to testify at 1000 EST/1500 GMT and his prepared remarks will be followed by a period of questions and answers.
The bidding deadline for the $12.5 in five-year Treasury notes is 1300 EST/1800 GMT.

"How the auction goes depends on what Greenspan has to say," said Rupert. "If he's negative, the market might make large (price) concessions and the auction might go OK. If we don't back it up, the auction might be average to mediocre."

"The Greenspan testimony comes before the auction so you're going to have the market reaction to his talk before the (1300 EST/1800 GMT) five-year auction (deadline for bids)," said James Blumenthal, economist at MMS International. "The auction outcome will be sensitive to what Greenspan syas because the market will have been sensitive to what he says."
Like most analysts, Blumenthal does not expect Greenspan to tread in areas where he has not tread before.
"We don't really look for anything new," said Blumenthal. "He'll say that the Fed must remain vigilant on inflation. He'll discuss the tight labor market."
At the short end of the maturity curve, three-month bill rates were unchanged at 5.02 percent. Six-month rates were up 1/32 to five percent. Year bill rates were up one basis point to 5.21 percent.
Two-year notes were down 1/32 to 99-30/32, yielding 5.91 percent. Ten-year notes were down 1/32 to 98-30/32, yielding 6.40 percent.
